transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Li (Redwood SE), Dr. Rina Shah (Curio Head of ML), Ezra Gomez (Infra Lead), Marta Silva (PM)

Auto summary (auto-generated): Discussed proof-of-concept scope to validate reserved capacity with burst. Focus on latency SLO 95th p95 <= 280ms for short prompts, cost target <$0.05 per 1k tokens after batching, fallback to cheaper model family during sustained peak. Agree next steps: send pricing, load harness, and token histograms.

Transcript body:
[00:00:02] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Rina, Marta, Ezra, you there?
[00:00:08] Rina: Yeah hi, thanks, we can hear you.
[00:00:11] Maya: Great. Quick round, I'll let Jonas jump in on the technical side. Today we want to scope a 4-week pilot to test reserved GPUs with burst and fallback policies. Main things we need are success criteria, workload shape and bench plan.
[00:00:28] Jonas: Hi all. Quick note on nomenclature real fast — when I say reserved pool I'm referring to a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) and burst is the temporary extra capacity Redwood can route to, correct?
[00:00:36] Rina: Yes that's right. For us reserved pool is important for deterministic latency for clinical workflows.
[00:00:42] Marta: And we need a fallback path because we can't have downtime during day shifts, so cost can spike but availability can't drop.
[00:00:49] Jonas: Understood. So typical pattern we recommend: baseline reserved capacity sized for 95th percentile, and burst configured for sustained 10-15 minute peaks. For longer sustained peaks the policy either autoscale the reserved or gracefully fallback to a quantized cheaper model.
[00:01:04] Ezra: How do you define 95 percentile here? Is it by QPS, tokens, or latency buckets?
[00:01:09] Jonas: Good question. Ideally by p95 latency per route — we usually map it to token distribution. If you can give us a 7-day token histogram per route we can recommend pool size.
[00:01:18] Rina: We have that, but it hasn't been extracted into per-route yet. We can pull it, it's in our internal logs.
[00:01:23] Marta: Also timeline, can we get benchmarks within first two weeks?
[00:01:27] Maya: Yes that's doable. We propose a smoke run immediately (2 hours) to validate baseline, then a controlled load test simulating bursts.
[00:01:33] Jonas: For the smoke run we'll use a small reserved pool mimicking 2 x A10 equiv, run 50-200 concurrent sessions with the sample prompts you give. We'll export p50/p95/p99, token costs and KV cache hit rates.
[00:01:46] Rina: A10 equiv? We're on-prem with A100 in prod, but our dev env is smaller. Does that mismatch affect results?
[00:01:53] Jonas: It does, we'll normalize by tokens/sec and model throughput in our report. If you want we can run comparative runs on both types, but that adds time.
[00:02:01] Ezra: What's the fallback mechanism? If reserved is saturated do you queue? Redirect?
[00:02:06] Jonas: We do a few things: first, soft queuing with a short TTL for user interactive flows, second fallback to a smaller model family (e.g., quantized LlamaX-2 equivalent) for non-critical or background tasks, third route to hosted higher-latency cheaper instances with degraded SLO. You can tune policy by route.
[00:02:24] Marta: For clinical inference, queuing is risky. We need deterministic behavior, so fallback to a slightly cheaper but still acceptable model is preferred.
[00:02:31] Rina: Agree. Success criteria for us: p95 latency <= 280ms for baseline reserved on short prompts (under 256 tokens), and fidelity delta < 2% on core eval prompts when using fallback model. Cost target of <$0.05 per 1k tokens across typical usage after batching.
[00:02:47] Maya: Perfect, that's specific — we'll map that back to pool sizing.
[00:02:51] Jonas: On batching/caching: prefix KV cache can cut tokens for repeated dialogs by 30-60% depending on repetition. We'll include caching config suggestions.
[00:02:59] Ezra: We've seen K-V cache referred to as K V cash in some logs — little typos, ha — but yeah we use local cache on our side too.
[00:03:07] Jonas: (chuckles) transcription got it wrong sometimes.
[00:03:10] Marta: Security question — we need guaranteed isolation for PHI, can Redwood run private vell? I mean VPC?
[00:03:18] Maya: Yes, Private deployment options exist. For this POC we can run dedicated pool with VPC peering and KMS integration. We'll share the security appendix.
[00:03:26] Rina: SOC2 scope — do you have an SOC2 report?
[00:03:29] Maya: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 type II and the security deck.
[00:03:33] Jonas: Back to sizing — if you can provide token histograms, average prompt lengths, and peak hourly QPS per route, we can propose a reserved pool sized to hit your p95 target and recommend burst capacity and fallback models.
[00:03:46] Rina: I'll pull that. Also, what about cold start for KV cache — does it impact p95 badly?
[00:03:52] Jonas: Cold starts can add 20-40ms depending on model and kernel priming. We account for kernel warmup in our baseline config.
[00:03:59] Marta: Can we have canary rollouts between fallback policies? Want to test fidelity impact on a small set first.
[00:04:04] Jonas: Absolutely. We support canary / A/B deploys with traffic split and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade past threshold. We'll instrument evals as part of the bench.
[00:04:13] Rina: On the bench, will you simulate real user prompts or synthetic ones?
[00:04:17] Jonas: Prefer real prompts — you can obscure PHI — but synthetic can augment tails. For fidelity we'll run your eval set against baseline and fallback models and produce ROUGE/BLEU or task-specific metric.
[00:04:29] Marta: What's the expected cost of the 4-week pilot? Do you have a ballpark?
[00:04:33] Maya: We'll send structured pricing. Ballpark: depends on reserved tier; initial small reserved + limited burst for benchmarks usually in low tens of thousands USD for full-featured pilot with monitoring — I'll confirm exact tiers in the email.
[00:04:46] Rina: That's in range. Ok around benchmarks — how long to get results?
[00:04:50] Jonas: Smoke run results within same day, detailed bench and report within 5 business days of full load tests. For the 4-week POC we'll run iterative tests at week 1 and week 3.
[00:04:59] Ezra: Network egress and data residency — for some EU patients we need data not to leave EU. Can you pin endpoints?
[00:05:05] Maya: Yes regional routing and private deployment can keep data in-region. We'll note that in the security appendix.
[00:05:11] Marta: Are there any gotchas re: quantized models and hallucination risk?
[00:05:15] Jonas: Quantized models can have slight shifts. That's why fidelity evals are part of success criteria. For the pilot we'll include prompt-level regression tests to flag any unacceptable deltas.
[00:05:25] Rina: Good. On the autoscale policy we'd like an aggressive burst for 10 minutes with throttling after 20 minutes — then either spin up more reserved or kick fallback. Can you implement a TTL-based escalation?
[00:05:36] Jonas: Yes TTL based escalation is standard — policy options: immediate fallback after X seconds, or queue until Y seconds, or escalate to reserved after Z minutes. We'll propose defaults but you can tune them by route.
[00:05:48] Maya: I'll note the specific numbers you suggested and include them in the POC runbook.
[00:05:52] Marta: Anything else on observability? We want per-token cost, per-route latency, and trace sampling.
[00:05:58] Jonas: Redwood Console gives token-level cost and per-model tracing hooks. We'll enable higher sampling for the pilot.
[00:06:04] Rina: Cool.
[00:06:06] Maya: Ok let's recap — action items: Redwood sends pricing + security appendix + load harness; Curio exports token histograms and confirms PII handling constraints; schedule smoke run next week. Any objections?
[00:06:20] Rina: No objections. Sounds good.
[00:06:22] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite for 2026-11-12 kickoff.
[00:06:29] Marta: Thanks.
[00:06:31] Ezra: Thanks all.
[00:06:34] Jonas: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names, some filler words, and a couple of overlapping speak segments.
notes: Customer prioritizes deterministic latency for clinical workflows.
Fallback must preserve >98% fidelity on core tasks.
Security and regional data residency are gating items for production.
